cards.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, is writing to the twelve tribes scattered abroad (James 1:1). He's just told his brothers to quit playing favorites with the rich and dishonoring the poor (James 2:1-6). Now he asks them what good it is if someone claims to have faith but has no deeds.

cards.question: Someone claims to have faith but has no deeds. James asks a follow-up question about that kind of faith. What does he want to know?

cards.text: Then James paints a picture, and it's not a pretty one. Suppose a brother or sister is without clothes and daily food.

And what if one of you just tells him, 'Go in peace; stay warm and well fed,' but doesn't provide for his physical needs? That's like texting a thumbs-up emoji to a friend whose car just died on the highway, and WOW, he's gonna ride that emoji ALL the way home!

cards.question: A brother or sister has no clothes and no daily food, and all they get from you is warm words. What good does James say that does?
James ties his picture back to faith. Faith by itself, if it does not result in action, is ___.

cards.text: Then James lets someone argue back: 'You have faith and I have deeds.' Like faith and deeds are toppings at my bakery, and you just pick sprinkles OR chocolate chips.

cards.question: James says someone will say, 'You have faith and I have deeds.' How does James answer?

answers.text: He'll show his faith by his deeds

cards.text: Then James says, 'You believe that God is one. Good for you!' Friend, I think that 'Good for you!' comes with a raised eyebrow, and I know a thing or two about eyebrows.

cards.question: Believing that God is one is good. But James says even the ___ believe that, and shudder.

cards.text: James keeps going, and now he gets direct: 'O foolish man, do you want evidence that faith without deeds is worthless?' Ohhh, James is bringing RECEIPTS.

cards.question: James brings out his evidence that faith without deeds is worthless. Who does he call our father?

cards.text: Abraham! James goes straight to the top and says Abraham was justified by what he did.

cards.question: James says Abraham was justified by what he did. What did Abraham do?

answers.text: Offered his son Isaac on the altar
Gave all he had to the poor
Built a temple for the LORD

cards.text: James says Abraham's faith was working with his actions. Friend, dough with no oven isn't a cookie, it's just a STICKY situation.

cards.question: Abraham's faith and his actions worked together. James says his faith was ___ by what he did.

cards.text: And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, 'Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness,' straight out of Genesis 15:6.

cards.question: True or false: Abraham was called a friend of God.
True or false: After Abraham's example, James says a man is justified by faith alone.

cards.text: Then James says, 'In the same way,' and I bet nobody saw his next name coming. Rahab the prostitute, a woman of Jericho (Joshua 2:1), was justified by her actions too!

cards.question: James says Rahab was justified by her actions. What did Rahab do?

answers.text: Welcomed the spies and sent them another way
Hid the ark and kept it safe
Fed the prophets hiding in a cave

cards.text: James wraps it up with one last picture, one every one of us knows: a body without the spirit.

cards.question: James ends with a picture of a body without the spirit. What does he say that body and faith without deeds have in common?

findings.problem: The blank asks for the unseen word "demons" in James's sentence. Card 9 gives no basis for reasoning that demons, rather than Romans or Gentiles, believe and shudder, so this tests luck or recall of wording instead of a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Four of the seven choice cards are discovery guesses without enough context to reason toward an answer: card 2 asks Abraham's identity, card 4 asks what Abraham did, card 8 asks whether he was called God's friend, and card 11 asks what Rahab did. Only cards 6, 9 and 13 offer an informed basis for a pick, so most of this stop's choices are not informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
